title: Duha, the forenoon prayer
hook: a voluntary prayer when the sun is up
carry: two units of duha thank every joint

segments.voice: Yesterday, tahajjud: the night prayer, a gift on top of the duty. Now the sun comes up.

"By the morning hours." That's how Pickthall opens surah ninety-three, and the Arabic word behind those morning hours is today's word. Duha is not dawn. Dawn has its prayer, fajr, prayed in the gray before sunrise. Duha comes later: the sun fully up, the commute done, the first coffee gone, the inbox filling. The middle of the morning, the stretch easiest to stop noticing. Islam puts a prayer there too, and nobody is required to pray it.
screen: `BY THE MORNING HOURS.` → `NOT DAWN: LATER.` → `NOBODY IS REQUIRED TO PRAY IT.`

segments.voice: Duha is a voluntary prayer, prayed after the sun has risen well into the sky and before the heat of noon. Its smallest form is two units. First, the hour has a surah. Surah ninety-three swears by the morning hours and the stillness of the night, then tells the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ that his Lord has not left him. A report in Sahih al-Bukhari ties it to a time when he had fallen ill and missed his night prayers, and someone taunted him that he'd been abandoned. So the forenoon, in that surah, is a sign of being remembered. Second, a hadith in Sahih Muslim gives the prayer a surprising job. Every morning, it says, a charity is owed for each joint of your body. Every glorifying of God is a charity, every word of praise, every good deed urged and every wrong discouraged. And two units prayed in the forenoon are enough for all of it. Your knuckles, your knees, your jaw: two units cover the thanks. Third, a witness. Umm Hani reported that on the day Mecca was opened, he bathed in her house and prayed eight units in the forenoon, lighter than any prayer she'd seen from him, yet with full bowing and prostration. Fourth, the timing has a picture. Another report in Sahih Muslim calls it the prayer of those who often turn back to God, and says its time is when the young camels feel the heat of the sand. Scholars give the window in hours and minutes now; the hadith gives it in hot sand.
screen: `THE HOUR HAS A SURAH.` · `A CHARITY FOR EVERY JOINT.` · `UMM HANI SAW EIGHT.` · `WHEN YOUNG CAMELS FEEL THE HEAT.`

segments.voice: Slowly open and close your hands, roll your shoulders, flex your feet: each joint is one of the charities the hadith counts. If you pray, you can plan two units of duha for later this morning, or pray them now if the sun is up. If you don't, let each joint you move be one thank-you, said without words.
Duha. The forenoon, when the sun is well up, and the voluntary prayer prayed in it. Today's word.
Your line: two units of duha thank every joint. The morning is remembered, and so are you. That's today, done.

howItsDone: Muslims who keep the duha prayer pray at least two voluntary units after the sun has risen well and before the time of the noon prayer, often at work, at home, or in the mosque after a morning class.

The occasion of surah 93 is restated closer to Bukhari 4950 (illness, missed night prayers, a taunt of abandonment) instead of 'revelation had paused and people mocked him'. Pickthall 93:1 quoted from memory as 'By the morning hours'; confirm.

Muslim 720 (charity on every joint; two rak'ahs of duha suffice) paraphrased; Bukhari 1981 (Abu Hurayrah's three counsels) paraphrased; the counts 'three days' and 'three things' come from that hadith.
Muslim 748 (salat al-awwabin when the young camels feel the heat) is stated as being about duha; confirm the identification is acceptable across schools.
'Its smallest form is two units' and the window 'after the sun has risen well ... before noon' reflect common fiqh; confirm. Larger numbers of units (e.g. Umm Hani's report) deliberately left out.
